meta.title: PathAble
meta.description: Barrier-aware walking routes for North York that show what is actually known about each sidewalk: verified, barrier, reported or no data.

landing.title: A city without limits begins with a better route.
landing.lede: Walking routes ranked by what is actually known about each sidewalk, with accessible transit when it helps.
landing.pilot: North York pilot. Outside North York we say so instead of guessing.

how.title: How it works
how.lede: Four steps, the same ones the planner walks you through.
how.s1Body: Your slope, width and curb limits.
how.s2Body: Search, tap the map or paste coordinates.
how.s3Body: See what is known about every stretch, and when the bus is faster.
how.s4Body: Turn-by-turn guidance that follows you, with voice if you want it.
how.exampleCaption: Route A from York University to Finch West, computed from North York open data.

states.title: Four knowledge states, never blurred
states.lede: Every stretch of every route is one of these. No data is never shown as accessible.
states.exampleLabel: Example stretch near Finch West station
states.mapLabel: Demo corridor with the selected state highlighted

reporting.title: Reports from people who were there
reporting.body: Photos have location data removed on your device before anything is sent. Reports stay marked as reported until a reviewer verifies them.
reporting.ai: Automatic photo analysis is turned off until a model passes our published evaluation. Until then, a person reviews every report.
reporting.removedTitle: Removed on your device before anything is sent

removed.time: Date and time the photo was taken
removed.camera: Camera make, model and serial number

reporting.kept: The image itself, resized to at most 1,600 pixels on its longest side
reporting.aiOff: Off. No model has passed evaluation.

winter.title: Winter is a different city
winter.body: Snow, ice and plowed-in ramps change daily. Winter markers come only from on-the-ground reports, show when they were seen and expire after 48 hours. Weather forecasts are never shown as sidewalk conditions.
winter.exampleLabel: Example of how a winter report appears. Not a real report.

trust.title: What we know, and how well
trust.body: In the York University to Yonge and Sheppard corridor, with a 5% slope limit and a 1.5 m minimum width, about 10% of walkable length is known accessible, 12% is a known barrier and 78% has no data. We publish how we measured that.
trust.sources: Sources: OpenStreetMap, City of Toronto Open Data, Natural Resources Canada lidar.
trust.corridorLabel: Demo corridor by walkable length, 5% slope limit and 1.5 m minimum width

coverage.title: Coverage and data status
coverage.lede: PathAble covers North York, the former municipality in Toronto’s north. Everything below is measured by the pipeline in our repository and dated; nothing is estimated by hand.
coverage.statusTitle: What we know, attribute by attribute
coverage.presenceValue: OpenStreetMap represents {pct}% of the City inventory’s {km} km of sidewalk sides
coverage.widthValue: {pct}% of sidewalk length; median error {err} m against mapped widths
coverage.slopeValue: {pct}% of corridor length where two lidar surveys agree
coverage.crossSlopeValue: Not measurable from a 1 m terrain model
coverage.kerbsValue: {pct}% of crossings have both ends mapped
coverage.mapAlt: Map of North York neighbourhoods shaded by how much of the City’s sidewalk inventory OpenStreetMap represents. Most neighbourhoods are above 80%; Humber Summit is lowest at about 41%.
coverage.outsideBody: Requests outside the pilot area return “outside coverage” and the planner says so. We do not show routes we cannot describe.
